title: The Oracle of the Old Library
logline: An Oracle that answers any question has started lying. Repair the library it reads from, and you repair the Oracle.
artStyle: Candlelit 2D pixel-painting, dark oak and parchment, warm gold rim light, soft blue glow from the Oracle. Top-down 3/4 view, 1600x900 scenes.

cast.name: The Archivist
cast.persona: Keeper of the stacks. Dry, precise, allergic to hand-waving. Explains by contrast: shows you the broken version first, then the fix. Calls scrolls 'documents' when annoyed.

cast.name: The Oracle
cast.persona: A voice in the blue flame that can only say what it was just handed. Confident even when starved of facts — which is exactly the problem. Never admits it is guessing unless shown the gap.

acts.title: Torn Scrolls
acts.goal: The night winds tore every scroll at a different place. Re-cut the scrolls so a single piece still holds a whole answer, then hand one to the Oracle.

prediction.question: You cut the scrolls into 40-word pieces. The answer to 'what dose did the Archivist record?' spans two sentences. What does the Oracle say?
options: The full answer — small pieces are always more precise
Half the answer, confidently, because the piece it got was cut mid-fact
Nothing — it refuses when a piece is too small

acts.explainAfter: A chunk is the smallest thing retrieval can hand over. Cut smaller than a fact and no single chunk can answer the question, so the Oracle completes it from habit instead. Overlap is cheap insurance: it re-staples the seam so a fact cut in half still survives in one piece.

dialogue.speaker: The Archivist
dialogue.line: The wind took every scroll on the east shelf. Cut them back yourself.

dialogue.speaker: The Oracle
dialogue.line: A dose of forty. I am certain of it.

dialogue.speaker: The Archivist
dialogue.line: Forty what? The unit is on the table behind you.

mechanic.question: What dose did the Archivist record, and when?
mechanic.goldFact: forty milligrams, taken at dusk on the third night

acts.title: The Oracle's Satchel
acts.goal: The Oracle will only read what fits in its satchel. Tune how many scrolls you stuff in — too few and the fact is missing, too many and the truth drowns in neighbours.

prediction.question: You raise k from 3 to 8 without reranking. The gold scroll is still in there. What happens to the answer?
options: Strictly better — more context can only help
Unchanged — the Oracle ignores anything irrelevant
Worse — five plausible neighbours give it new claims to borrow

acts.explainAfter: k is a budget, not a volume knob. Every extra scroll is one more thing the Oracle is allowed to believe. Reranking lets you keep the budget small and still land the gold scroll on top — fewer, better scrolls beat more, noisier ones.

dialogue.speaker: The Archivist
dialogue.line: It will read whatever fits in the satchel. All of it. Equally.

dialogue.speaker: The Oracle
dialogue.line: Forty milligrams, reduced from sixty, halved for younger readers.

dialogue.speaker: The Archivist
dialogue.line: Two of those three came from scrolls about a different library.

mechanic.question: What dose did the Archivist record, and when?
mechanic.goldFact: forty milligrams, taken at dusk on the third night

acts.title: The Lying Oracle
acts.goal: The Oracle has just stated a dose nobody ever wrote down. Interrogate it, make it point at the scroll each claim came from, and strike the claim with no scroll behind it.

prediction.question: Every retrieved scroll is relevant and the answer sounds perfect. Is it grounded?
options: Yes — relevant scrolls guarantee a grounded answer
Not necessarily — a claim can still appear that no scroll supports
Only if the scrolls are ranked

acts.explainAfter: Grounding is a per-claim property, not a per-answer vibe. Retrieval decides what the Oracle *could* say; grounding checks what it *did* say, sentence by sentence, against the scrolls it was handed. Anything that cannot point at a scroll is a guess wearing a confident voice.

dialogue.speaker: The Oracle
dialogue.line: Forty milligrams at dusk. The Binder approved the change himself.

dialogue.speaker: The Archivist
dialogue.line: Show me the scroll that says so.

dialogue.speaker: The Oracle
dialogue.line: I have no scroll for the second part.

mechanic.question: What dose did the Archivist record, and who approved it?
mechanic.goldFact: forty milligrams, taken at dusk on the third night; no scroll records who approved it
